Magical gene / lines and strokes

Filigree

White metalwork over the muscle masses - a closed spiral on each of them, long arcs following the body's contours, and broken tracks of short dashes filling the space between.

What it does

FiligreeThree element forms at once, all hard-edged and all the same white: closed spirals of about two turns, one to each major muscle mass; long shallow arcs following the contour of the zone they sit in; and fields of short dashes lying parallel to the nearest arc, in broken tracks. The dashes crowd along the topline and the back edges of the shoulder and hindquarter and thin to isolated marks at the belly. The two sides are not mirrored, and the spirals do not all turn the same way. Nothing on the head, nothing below the knee.
Coloured filigreeThe same metalwork worked in a colour rather than in white - the shade runs in a line of horses. Fully recessive: two copies, and a single copy beside the white allele shows white. It never gives blue eyes.
Wild typeNo filigree.

What you can get

Finding one

About 1 in 1,786 wild horses is born showing this. That is the whole of the supply: catch one, or make one with the carrot below. Breeds set their own pools and a breed built around this gene will carry it far more often than the wild population does.

Its gene carrot

The file

common/src/main/resources/horsegenetics/genes/filigree.json — a data-driven gene, not a Java class. It is listed in the index.json beside it and registered by Genes' class initialiser at startup.

Keyhorsegenetics.filigree
Phasemagical — it adds signed colour in phase 3, after the pigment has resolved
Priority367 — where it sits in the one (priority, key) paint order
AllelesFlg · Flc · n
Varies per horse3 values drawn once off the expressing allele copy, so a foal that inherits the copy inherits the look
Built fromAXIS, SPECKLE, SPIRAL, STROKES, TOWARD

What it paints

Filigree

  1. one spiral to each muscle mass — SPIRAL, painted with TOWARD
  2. long arcs along the contours — STROKES, painted with TOWARD
  3. dash fields between and along the arcs — STROKES × SPECKLE × AXIS, painted with TOWARD
  4. the same work reaching onto the upper legs — STROKES × AXIS, painted with TOWARD

Coloured filigree

  1. one coloured spiral to each muscle mass — SPIRAL, painted with TOWARD
  2. long coloured arcs along the contours — STROKES, painted with TOWARD
  3. coloured dash fields between the arcs — STROKES × SPECKLE × AXIS, painted with TOWARD
